elements_not_encoded.text: If abdominal aortic aneurysm likely: avoid giving IV fluids even if BP < 90/60 (raising blood pressure may worsen rupture).
If BP < 90/60 or pancreatitis likely, give sodium chloride 0.9% 500mL IV over 30 minutes, repeat until systolic BP > 90. Continue 1L 6 hourly. Stop if breathing
If complicated pyelonephritis likely: first collect urine for MCS and then give ceftriaxone 1g IV2/IM.
If kidney stone likely: give sodium chloride 0.9% 1L IV 6 hourly. If pain severe, give morphine 5-10mg IM or diluted morphine 3-5mg IV. If giving IV, dilute 10m
If patient known to have cancer, refer same day.

judgment_calls.decision: No SNOMED concept for complicated pyelonephritis; the probable rule diagnoses Acute pyelonephritis and the Urgent rule restates the criteria (flank pain, leucocytes/nitrites, any complicating factor) instead of using active_condition, because uncomplicated pyelonephritis shares the concept.
judgment_calls.alternatives: active_condition Acute pyelonephritis in the priority rule (would make uncomplicated pyelonephritis urgent).

judgment_calls.decision: Probable Mechanical low back pain needs Backache, every Q1/Q2/Q3 item explicitly answered No, and onset within 6 weeks. Age criteria cannot be expressed.
judgment_calls.alternatives: Backache alone (fires for patients with red-flag answers too).

judgment_calls.alternatives: Axial spondyloarthritis or Arthritis of spine (a different, narrower diagnosis).
